Two columns stand out as candidate leaks: log_target_v2 (spearman 0.9990 with the target) and near_target_proxy (pearson 0.9987). Both are essentially deterministic transforms of the target, so any model given them can reconstruct the label and score a perfect r2. Every other feature is noise-level (|correlation| <= 0.040), confirming one of these two columns is doing all the work. The perfect_match_rate of 0.0 only rules out an exact row-duplicate target copy — it does not rule out a near-perfect monotone/linear proxy, which both candidates are. Note the naming itself is a red flag: 'log_target_v2' hard-codes the target in its name and 'near_target_proxy' literally suggests a proxy. Report the metric as leaked and drop both columns before any evaluation.

Verdict: leakage — drop both proxy columns and re-train/re-evaluate.
